snapshot.nextjs-advisories: [2026-07-20] MATERIAL, NEW: Next.js launched a formal monthly security-release program; its first scheduled release targeted 2026-07-20 (today) with coordinated patches for the 16.2.x and 15.5.x lines — 4 high + 5 medium severity fixes. Advance-notice model: exact GHSA IDs/fixed versions publish only when the patch ships, not retrievable at scan time (direct advisories-page WebFetch still only showed the May 6-7 batch, likely not yet re-indexed). Distinct from the already-ticketed May batch (BIN-213). Binge's package-lock.json resolves next@16.2.9 — inside the affected line. Filed as GitHub issue #44. (WebFetch direct + WebSearch corroboration across gbhackers/cybersecuritynews/digitalapplied/cyberpress.)
snapshot.ghsa-npm: [2026-07-20] No Next.js/React/Firebase JS SDK/firebase-functions advisories surfaced in the general npm feed this cycle (the new Next.js July release isn't GHSA-indexed yet, see nextjs-advisories). Prior transitive-dep CVEs (protobufjs CVE-2026-41242, fast-xml-parser CVE-2026-25128) remain non-issues — Binge's resolved lockfile versions unchanged (protobufjs 7.6.4/7.5.6, fast-xml-parser 5.7.2), already past fix versions. No change since last scan.
snapshot.firebase-js-sdk-releases: [2026-07-20] Newest release still firebase@12.16.0 (2026-07-09) — no new release since last scan. No change to the 2026-07-13 analysis: Binge's src/lib/firebase/appCheck.ts passes an explicit new ReCaptchaV3Provider(siteKey), not Enterprise, so the 0.12.0 auto-init-Enterprise-provider behavior still doesn't apply. Installed version remains 12.12.1 (^12.12.1 range, confirmed in package-lock.json).
snapshot.firestore-rules-relnotes: [2026-07-20] Page's own 'last updated' still 2026-01-21 — unchanged since last scan. No rules-language change this cycle. (WebFetch 403'd; WebSearch fallback used.)
snapshot.recaptcha-enterprise-relnotes: [2026-07-20] No v3-breaking change found this cycle; WebSearch surfaced only pre-existing/generic context (mobile WAF GA, fraud-prevention features, execute/getClient timeout param) — nothing new affecting Binge's ReCaptchaV3Provider usage. (WebFetch 403'd; WebSearch fallback used.)
snapshot.gh-changelog-dependabot: [2026-07-20] New entry since last scan: 'Default Package Cooldown' (2026-07-14) — Dependabot now waits 3+ days after a release before opening a version-update PR by default (security-update PRs still open immediately, unaffected). Binge's .github/dependabot.yml does use weekly npm version updates, so this will shift when non-security Dependabot PRs land by a few days — but it's a zero-config default with no security-path impact, so non-actionable; no ticket filed. (WebFetch 403'd; WebSearch fallback used.)
